 GAMEDAY: Senators at Jets
 7:00 pm CDT; TV - TSN 3; Radio - 680 CJOB/Power97
 By 
 Jamie Thomas 
 WinnipegJets.com 
 November 17, 2026 
 Link copied 
 WINNIPEG – Through 21 games of their 84-game schedule, the Winnipeg Jets have officially reached the quarter pole of the 2026-27 season. And considering everything this team has already experienced, it feels like they've packed the equivalent of half a season into those first 21 games.
 As they prepare to open a four-game homestand tonight against the Ottawa Senators, the Jets have won six straight with two four-goal comeback victories on either end of the streak. Josh Morrissey believes the team has done a great job blocking the outside noise.
 “We've done a really good job with that. So, we’ve found ways to win. The Montreal game is different I think because we were playing such a good game. The last game first 30 minutes, didn't love our game but again, it's just something we can draw on that we're resilient and we're never out of it,” said Morrissey.
 “That's a quality that it's kind of hard to acquire and something that I think we've shown to ourselves that we can be resilient.”
 With a four-point outing in Chicago on Saturday, Mark Scheifele cemented his place in the Jets franchise record books, passing Dale Hawerchuk for the most career points in franchise history (933) before passing Thomas Steen for the franchise assist record later in the game. Scheifele needs one more goal to pass Hawerchuk for the franchise goals record with his 380th career goal.
 "It was pretty special, especially to do it in a four-goal comeback," said Scheifele.
 "So, it was really special to be able to enjoy that night with even all the dads and Gregg. And it was obviously a fantastic night, and very very blessed to be a part of this group of guys."
 Morrissey got the primary assist on Scheifele’s goal that pushed him past Hawerchuk in the second period in Chicago.
 “It's just cool to think that coming in here as an 18-year-old, Scheif was kind of the leader of the young guys and we've grown up together. Obviously, KC, him and I came into the team at the same time,” said Morrissey.
 “Just growing up alongside those guys, they’re two of my best friends and just incredible players. I'm lucky I get to play with those guys every day, special to be a part of that goal.”
 As they start the second quarter of the season, they get two more Eastern Conference opponents in the Senators and Islanders.
 “We’ve got two more Eastern teams (on this homestand) and another Eastern road trip here. But the one sort of bright side looking at it is we are sort of done with the heavy hitters in the East,” said Scott Arniel.
 “We’ll be done with Boston and Jersey at the end of the month, we’re missing the Islanders, you throw Tampa, Florida, Carolina, Montreal in there. Really running into those teams early on, that means we’ll have a lot of games against the West.”
 The Senators belong to one of the most competitive divisions in the league right now in the Atlantic. Ottawa is tied with Tampa and Montreal for first with 28 points, Boston and Florida are right behind with 27 each. Arniel says tonight’s game with be a lot like the game Jets fans saw here a week ago against New Jersey.
 "They're fast, they're really good defending. They're a strong defending team, something they've built over the last couple of years there," said Arniel.
 "It's a good hockey club over there. They have the detail when it comes to their special teams and they have quickness and they forecheck hard, but they also defend real well in their end of the rink."
 It looks like from the morning skate that Henry Thrun will make his Jets debut tonight on the blueline, Thrun has played 123 games in the NHL with San Jose and Toronto.
 "Saw some video of him in the summertime, but at the end of the day, showed well in training camp," said Arniel.
 "We actually had him running our power play when we were, had a lot of a bunch of the kids in the first game. He's got some jump to him, got some offense to him, and then he's got some compete."
 UPDATE: We've recalled Danny Zhilkin from the @ManitobaMoose ✈️ pic.twitter.com/581ZhFb9F7 
— Winnipeg Jets (@NHLJets) November 17, 2026 
 Danny Zhilkin has been recalled and is on his way from Grand Rapids where the Manitoba Moose are scheduled to face the Griffins tonight. Arniel says Zhilkin has been the team’s best player so far this season.
 "I think at the end of the day, the one thing about Danny every year he's gotten better and better, and he's got an awful lot of confidence in his game, and this year he isn't just a defender," said Arniel.
 "He's down there. He's been scoring goals and making plays, and he's. I know he's something that Mo (Moose head coach Mark Morrison) really leans on in all situations."
 Stuart Skinner will start in goal tonight, Skinner has won his last six starts against the Ottawa Senators, last losing on Jan. 15, 2022. Skinner has a career record of 7-1-0 against Ottawa with a .902 save percentage and 2.72 goals against average.
 Puck drop is scheduled for 7 PM local time.
